subject: Combined Science
source: Edexcel (Pearson) GCSE (9-1) Combined Science 1SC0 specification (2016 onwards) — Y11 covered topics across Biology Topics 6–9, Chemistry Topics 5–9 and Physics Topics 8–15 with HT-only items flagged.

specPoints.specTitle: Biology — plant structures and transport: xylem, phloem, transpiration and translocation; factors affecting transpiration rate
Biology — photosynthesis: word and balanced symbol equations; factors affecting rate; uses of glucose
Biology — homeostasis: maintenance of body temperature, blood glucose, water and nitrogen balance
Biology — control of blood glucose by insulin and glucagon (HT only — full glucagon mechanism); Type 1 vs Type 2 diabetes
Biology — endocrine system: glands and key hormones; menstrual cycle hormones; methods of contraception
Biology — gas exchange: alveoli, respiration link; circulatory system: heart, blood vessels, blood components
Biology — coronary heart disease and treatments (stents, statins); lifestyle factors and risk
Biology — ecosystems and material cycles: biotic/abiotic factors, food webs, energy transfer; carbon and water cycles
Biology — biodiversity, eutrophication, decomposition; required practical investigating decomposition rate
Chemistry — quantitative chemistry: relative formula mass, conservation of mass, reacting masses (HT only — moles, concentrations and limiting reactants)
Chemistry — concentrations of solutions in g/dm³ and mol/dm³ (HT for mol/dm³); titration calculations (HT only)
Chemistry — percentage yield, atom economy and reasoning about industrial processes
Chemistry — Group 1, Group 7 and Group 0 trends; displacement reactions; transition metals overview
Chemistry — rates of reaction: collision theory; effect of concentration, temperature, surface area, catalysts
Chemistry — energy changes: exothermic and endothermic reactions; reaction profiles; bond energy calculations (HT only)
Chemistry — fuels: combustion of hydrocarbons; cracking; environmental impact of fuels
Chemistry — Earth's atmosphere over time; greenhouse gases and global warming; human contributions and mitigation
Chemistry — separate chemistry: identifying ions by precipitation and flame tests; testing for hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and chlorine gases
Physics — energy resources and transfers; efficiency; renewable vs non-renewable resources
Physics — forces and elasticity: Hooke's law F = ke; elastic energy ½ke²; limit of proportionality; required practical with springs
Physics — vector and scalar quantities; resultant forces and equilibrium
Physics — current, potential difference and resistance; series and parallel circuits; Ohm's law and I-V characteristics
Physics — mains electricity: ac vs dc; UK supply; structure of three-core cables; energy transfer P = VI = I²R
Physics — National Grid: step-up and step-down transformers; high-voltage transmission to reduce energy losses (HT only — quantitative reasoning)
Physics — static electricity: charging by friction; attraction/repulsion of charges; electric fields (HT only — field-line representation)
Physics — magnetism: permanent and induced magnets; magnetic field patterns; the Earth's magnetic field
Physics — motor effect: force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field; Fleming's left-hand rule; force F = BIL (HT only)
Physics — particle model of matter: density of materials; changes of state; specific heat capacity ΔE = mcΔθ; specific latent heat E = mL
Physics — particle motion in gases: temperature and pressure; gas pressure-volume relationship pV = constant (HT only)
Physics — forces and matter: deformation, elastic vs inelastic; relationship between force and extension
